messages:
perf-bot: NIGHTLY ALERT: model-x-small serving p50 latency +22% vs baseline in us-west at 03:02 UTC. Metric group: runtime/latencty/p50. Trigger threshold: 15%. Link: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/alerts/1972

sam: ugh, I saw that spike in the dashboard this morning. We had a rollout last night: release 2026-03-15-23:40 (includes PR #4123 by @jia).

jia: confirmed, PR #4123 touched kernel selection and batching heuristics. I added a heuristic to prefer fused-attention kernels when seq_len <= 64, and a small batching boundary change to prefer larger batch windows.

oliver: CI perf job for nightly-e2e flagged a regression too: https://ci.redwood/flows/98765 — p50 increased 18% in the perf-check job. CI job output attached.

ci-bot: PERF CHECK FAILED: job nightly-e2e (build 98765). p50 baseline=42ms current=50ms (+19%). See artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/98765/perf-report.html

nora: can someone run a quick bisect across the merge window? If it's #4123 we should either revert or roll forward a fix before we finish the day.

oliver: running git bisect now between tags v2026-03-14 and v2026-03-15. Quick note: suspect area runtime/kernel_selector.cpp and runtime/batching/scheduler.cpp

oliver: (output)
```
$ git bisect start v2026-03-15 v2026-03-14
Bisecting: 4 revisions left to test after this (roughly 2 steps)
[ab12c3d] heuristics: prefer fused-attn when seq<=64
  good: v2026-03-14
  bad: v2026-03-15
```

oliver: bisect narrowed it down to commit ab12c3d (PR #4123) — the fused-attn preference and batch window tweak are the only changes in the hot path.

jia: ack. I added a fast path for fused kernels but the selection code didn't account for latency variance when KV cache is hot vs cold. That could explain p50 swings depending on recent history. I also changed batch window from 8ms -> 12ms.

maria: interesting — I pulled traces and KV cache hit-rate dropped ~14% around the same time as the delta. Looks like larger batch window increased cold-start miss amplification on KV lookups, causing extra decode tokens and higher tail latency.

sam: so root cause theory: kernel selection + larger batch window => different scheduling that reduces effective KV hits -> more compute per request -> p50 regresses. Sounds plausible.

nora: immediate mitigations: 1) gate the fused-attn heuristic behind an env flag; 2) revert the batch window change; 3) push a hotfix that makes kernel selector consider KV cache hit-rate as a tie-breaker. Which do we do now?

jia: I can push a revert PR for the batching window right away. Revert diff is trivial. I'll also add a flag guard for fused-attn so we can disable it in prod while we ruggedly test.

deploy-bot: rollback requested: rollup/rollback-1718823500 created for service inference-runtime in us-west. Approvals required: 1.

sam: +1 from me for rollback of batch window and gating fused-attn. We should hold the rollout until we have perf regression test results from CI.

ci-bot: re-running perf-check with reverted batching window in a canary branch. Triggered job nightly-e2e-canary (build 98768).

ci-bot: JOB UPDATE: nightly-e2e-canary (98768) artifacts -> p50=43ms (+2% vs baseline). Diff looks within noise.

maria: KV hit-rate bounced back to baseline in canary traces. Looks like batching was the main amplifier. But keep the fused-attn flag disabled until we run full A/B with different seq distributions.

nora: action items: (1) @jia open PR to revert batch window (done) and add env flag for fused-attn (in progress). (2) @oliver add an automated perf check that simulates KV-hot vs KV-cold workloads in CI. (3) @sam coordinate a controlled rollout after 48h observation window.

sam: noted. I'll also add a dashboard annotation for the 2026-03-15 rollout to help future triage. Thanks everyone, great fast reaction. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: p50 returned within thresholds at 03:50 UTC after canary rollback. Monitoring will continue.
